w:r.w:t: Connecting Validation Intelligence to the Live Execution Loop

The Erector (Prompt 3) ends at blueprint launch. The execution loop (Prompt 5 onward) begins at task generation. This prompt builds the bridge between them. Without this bridge, the archetype intelligence gathered during validation is collected but never used. The first week plan is generated but never seeded. The reality score is stored but the execution engine never reads it.
This prompt has one job: make the Erector's output a living, active part of every execution decision from the moment the blueprint launches.
Read services/validation/ completely — especially the path selection and first week plan outputs.
Read engines/blueprint/BlueprintEngine.ts — the launchBlueprint() function specifically. You will extend it, not replace it.
Read lib/bhudhi/ — the full prompt library. You will ADD registrations, not change existing ones.
Read app/(onboarding)/ and app/(validation)/ — map the current routing before touching any route file.
Read the Blueprint and Validation models in prisma/schema.prisma to confirm the fields added in Prompt 3 are present before building anything.
EXTEND ONLY. launchBlueprint() gets new logic added inside the existing transaction. Nothing is removed.
ARCHETYPE NEVER OVERRIDES CONDITION. Archetype multipliers adjust task count ranges and pace calculations. They never set a condition directly. Condition is always owned by the Signal Engine.
FIRST WEEK TASKS ARE SMOKE TESTS. They seed the task queue with reality-checking actions before the normal execution loop takes over. They do not replace the normal loop.
ALL NEW BHUDHI CALLS FOLLOW THE EXISTING PATTERN. Registered in TriggerRouter, Zod schema, BhudhiLog write, deterministic fallback. No exceptions.
D — WHAT TO BUILD (8 TASKS IN ORDER)

Add these fields to the Blueprint model in prisma/schema.prisma (all nullable). Run migration: npx prisma migrate dev --name add_archetype_intel_to_blueprint

The Task Generation Engine (TaskGenerationEngine) selects task types based on blueprint position and condition. Add industry_state as a context modifier that adjusts which task types are weighted higher during generation.

Task 6 — Harden onboarding → validation → dashboard routing
The routing sequence must be enforced at the server level, not just the client. Three checks are required:

CHECK 1 — Blueprint cannot launch without completed validation. In /api/v1/blueprints/launch, before processing: check that blueprint.validation_id is set AND the linked validation record has validation_stage = 'complete' AND selected_path is not null. If any check fails, return 400 with reason.

CHECK 2 — Validation screens cannot be accessed without an active blueprint draft. The app/(validation)/ layout must verify that blueprintDraftId exists in session/query params and is in status 'validating' before rendering any validation screen.

CHECK 3 — After blueprint launch, the redirect must go to /dashboard, not back to onboarding. Update the success handler in the Blueprint Level Selection screen to call the launch API then redirect to /dashboard.

GATE: Attempt to POST /api/v1/blueprints/launch with a blueprint that has no completed validation — receive 400 with 'validation_required' error. Attempt to access /validation/scores without a draft in session — receive redirect to /onboarding.
Task 7 — Add smoke_test to TaskType enum

The task seeding in Task 2 uses task_type = 'smoke_test'. Add this to the TaskType enum in prisma/schema.prisma and run the migration. The task generation engine and condition engine do not restrict smoke_test tasks — they always execute regardless of condition (except 'blocked' state).
smoke_test // NEW — Erector first week plan tasks
GATE: Migration runs without error. Seeded first week tasks have task_type = 'smoke_test'. Condition Engine does not block smoke_test tasks even in Danger condition.
Task 8 — Emit Erector events at launch

After the blueprint launches successfully, emit the erector_blueprint_launched event. This connects the Erector to the event system and allows future workers to react to validated launches differently from unvalidated ones.
